words.enDefinition: the October holiday often celebrated with costumes and treats

examples.en: Our neighbours put paper bats in their windows for Halloween every year.
examples.zh: 邻居每年都会为「万圣节前夜」在窗户上贴纸蝙蝠。

examples.en: I'd never celebrated Halloween before moving into the residence hall here.
examples.zh: 我搬进这里的宿舍以前，从来没有过「万圣节前夜」。

words.enDefinition: the evening when people celebrate Halloween with events and activities

examples.en: On Halloween night, we watched old films in our residence lounge.
examples.zh: 「万圣节之夜」，我们在宿舍休息室里看老电影。

examples.en: The students put out lanterns on Halloween night just before supper.
examples.zh: 「万圣节之夜」，同学们在晚饭前摆出了灯笼。

words.enDefinition: to visit homes in costume asking for Halloween treats

examples.en: My host family's kids invited me to go trick-or-treating with them.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的孩子邀请我和他们一起「挨家挨户讨糖」。

examples.en: Some children on our street go trick-or-treating before it gets dark.
examples.zh: 我们街上有些小孩在天黑前就去「挨家挨户讨糖」了。

words.enDefinition: the traditional greeting children say when asking for Halloween candy

examples.en: Kids shouted "Trick or treat!" when my roommate answered the door that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，室友一开门，孩子们就喊：「不给糖就捣蛋」！

examples.en: We heard "Trick or treat!" from the front steps before the doorbell rang.
examples.zh: 门铃响之前，我们就听见门前台阶上有人喊「不给糖就捣蛋」。

collocations: knock and say trick or treat

words.enDefinition: someone who visits houses to ask for Halloween candy

examples.en: The first trick-or-treater at our door wore a cardboard robot costume.
examples.zh: 第一个到门口的「万圣节讨糖人」穿着纸板机器人装。

examples.en: I put an extra piece of candy aside for the last trick-or-treater.
examples.zh: 我给最后一个「万圣节讨糖的人」多留了一颗糖。

words.enDefinition: an event where children collect treats at decorated parked cars

examples.en: My student club decorated a car for the campus trunk-or-treat.
examples.zh: 我们学生社团给一辆车做了装饰，准备参加校园的「汽车后备箱讨糖活动」。

examples.en: Families started lining up early at the trunk-or-treat by the library.
examples.zh: 来参加图书馆旁「汽车后备箱讨糖活动」的家庭很早就排起了队。

words.enDefinition: to hand sweets to children or visitors at an event

examples.en: I volunteered to give out candy while my housemates decorated the porch.
examples.zh: 室友们装饰门廊时，我自告奋勇去「分发糖果」。

examples.en: Families who wanted to give out candy set chairs by their doors.
examples.zh: 想「分发糖果」的人家把椅子放到了门边。

collocations: give out candy at the door

words.enDefinition: a bowl filled with sweets for people to take

examples.en: We put a candy bowl next to the pumpkin by the door.
examples.zh: 我们在门口的南瓜旁边放了个「装糖果的碗」。

examples.en: I refilled the candy bowl after a large group of children left.
examples.zh: 一大群小孩走后，我又往「装糖果的碗」里添了些糖。

words.enDefinition: sweets with a separate wrapper around each piece or serving

examples.en: The residence volunteers brought individually wrapped candy to share outside the common room.
examples.zh: 宿舍志愿者带了些「独立包装的糖果」，在公共休息室外分享。

examples.en: The bag of individually wrapped candy made it easy to refill our bowl.
examples.zh: 有了这一袋「独立包装的糖果」，往碗里添糖很方便。

words.enDefinition: asks each person to pick up only one item

examples.en: The note by the bowl read "Take one, please" in big letters.
examples.zh: 碗旁的纸条上用大字写着：「请只拿一个」。

examples.en: My roommate put "Take one per person" on the candy table sign.
examples.zh: 室友在糖果桌的牌子上写着「每人请只拿一个」。

collocations: bowl with a take one sign

words.enDefinition: a large amount of candy collected while trick-or-treating

examples.en: The kids dumped their candy haul on the floor after coming home.
examples.zh: 孩子们一回家，就把「讨到的一大堆糖果」倒在地上。

examples.en: My neighbour's son showed me his candy haul before heading inside.
examples.zh: 邻居家的孩子进屋前，给我看了他「讨到的一大堆糖果」。

words.enDefinition: to keep the light by the front door switched on

examples.en: We decided to leave the porch light on while we still had candy to give out.
examples.zh: 还有糖果可以分的时候，我们决定「让门廊灯亮着」。

examples.en: My host asked me to leave the porch light on until the kids came home.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的主人请我「让门廊灯亮着」，等孩子们回家。

collocations: remember to leave the porch light on
choose to leave the porch light on
leave the porch light on for visitors

words.enDefinition: having no candy left to hand out to visitors

examples.en: We were out of candy by the time my roommate got back from class.
examples.zh: 室友下课回来时，我们的「糖发完了」。

examples.en: The sign said "Out of candy," but the pumpkin was still glowing beside it.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「糖发完了」，旁边的南瓜灯还亮着。

words.enDefinition: going from one house or building to the next

examples.en: The club planned door-to-door trick-or-treating for the afternoon before the costume party.
examples.zh: 换装派对那天下午，社团安排了「挨家挨户」讨糖的活动。

examples.en: We stayed in the courtyard instead of joining the door-to-door group.
examples.zh: 我们留在院子里，没跟着那组人去「挨家挨户」讨糖。

words.enDefinition: slightly frightening because something seems strange or ghostly

examples.en: We put on some spooky music for the student film screening.
examples.zh: 学生电影放映时，我们放了点「让人觉得阴森」的音乐。

examples.en: The spooky paper shadows looked funny once we turned on the lights.
examples.zh: 灯一开，那些本来「阴森森的」纸影子看起来挺好笑的。

words.enDefinition: a walk-through attraction designed to make visitors feel frightened

examples.en: We took our classmates to a haunted house run by the theatre club.
examples.zh: 我们带同学去了戏剧社办的「鬼屋」。

examples.en: The haunted house used funny sound effects instead of anything too scary.
examples.zh: 「鬼屋」用了些好笑的音效，整体也没布置得太吓人。

words.enDefinition: a sudden moment intended to make people jump in fright

examples.en: I spilled popcorn during a jump scare at the Halloween film screening.
examples.zh: 万圣节电影放到一个「突然惊吓的桥段」，我把爆米花都洒了。

examples.en: My friend warned me about the jump scare just before the music stopped.
examples.zh: 音乐停下来之前，朋友就提醒我有个「突然惊吓的桥段」。

collocations: warn someone about a jump scare

words.enDefinition: a frightening story about a ghost or other unexplained events

examples.en: Our roommate told a ghost story about the oldest building on campus.
examples.zh: 室友讲了个校园里最老那栋楼的「鬼故事」。

examples.en: Nobody could finish the ghost story without laughing at the sound effects.
examples.zh: 音效太搞笑了，谁都没法忍住笑把「鬼故事」讲完。

words.enDefinition: decorative material made to look like webs spun by spiders

examples.en: We hung fake cobwebs over the bookshelf before our Halloween film night.
examples.zh: 万圣节电影之夜前，我们在书架上方挂了「假蜘蛛网」。

examples.en: Someone left fake cobwebs on the common room windows after the party.
examples.zh: 聚会结束后，有人把「假蜘蛛网」留在了公共休息室的窗上。

collocations: cover a doorway with fake cobwebs

words.enDefinition: bat shapes cut from paper and used as decorations

examples.en: We taped paper bats around the menu board in the student café.
examples.zh: 我们把「纸蝙蝠」贴在学生咖啡馆菜单板的四周。

examples.en: The club made paper bats from old black posters for the evening.
examples.zh: 社团用废旧的黑色海报做了些「纸蝙蝠」，晚上布置用。

collocations: put paper bats in the window

words.enDefinition: an ornament made to resemble a skeleton, often for Halloween

examples.en: The skeleton decoration kept falling off the student lounge door that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，学生休息室门上的「骷髅装饰」总往下掉。

examples.en: We tied a scarf around the skeleton decoration during the costume competition.
examples.zh: 化装比赛时，我们给「骷髅装饰」围了条围巾。

words.enDefinition: an arrangement of objects used to decorate a place for Halloween

examples.en: The library's Halloween display included pumpkins painted by first-year students last week.
examples.zh: 图书馆的「万圣节主题布景」里有大一学生上周涂绘的南瓜。

examples.en: We stopped to take pictures of a Halloween display across the street.
examples.zh: 我们停下来，给街对面的「万圣节主题布景」拍了几张照片。

words.enDefinition: the weeks around Halloween when spooky themes become popular

examples.en: Our film club picked three funny horror movies for spooky season this year.
examples.zh: 今年「万圣节前后的节庆季」，电影社挑了三部搞笑恐怖片。

examples.en: The students were already hanging bats in the lounge for spooky season.
examples.zh: 为了迎接「万圣节前后的节庆季」，同学们已经在休息室挂起蝙蝠装饰了。

words.enDefinition: a social gathering where people wear costumes instead of everyday clothes

examples.en: I borrowed a friend's hat for the costume party in our building.
examples.zh: 我借了朋友的帽子，准备参加楼里的「化装派对」。

examples.en: We left the costume party early to catch the last campus bus.
examples.zh: 为了坐上末班校园公交，我们提前离开了「化装派对」。

words.enDefinition: a competition that awards prizes for the costumes people wear

examples.en: My roommate entered the costume contest dressed as a tiny library cart.
examples.zh: 室友扮成一辆小图书推车参加了「化装比赛」。

examples.en: The costume contest took place after the last song of the evening.
examples.zh: 当晚最后一首歌结束后，举行了「化装比赛」。

words.enDefinition: indicates that people may attend without wearing a costume

examples.en: The invite said "Costume optional," so I wore my usual clothes and boots.
examples.zh: 邀请上说「可不穿化装服」，所以我穿了平时的衣服和靴子。

examples.en: I was glad to see "Costume optional," since my costume hadn't arrived.
examples.zh: 看见「可不穿化装服」我很高兴，因为我的化装服还没到。

words.enDefinition: to arrive at an event wearing clothes that form a costume

examples.en: We were invited to come in costume for the evening's pumpkin painting event.
examples.zh: 主办方邀请我们「穿化装服来」参加当晚的南瓜彩绘活动。

examples.en: I didn't plan to come in costume until my roommate offered me a cape.
examples.zh: 我本来没打算「穿化装服来」，后来室友说可以借我一件披风。

collocations: encourage guests to come in costume
ask everyone to come in costume

words.enDefinition: to put on clothing that makes you look like someone or something

examples.en: My desk mate wanted to dress up as a librarian from a novel.
examples.zh: 同桌想「装扮成」一部小说里的图书馆管理员。

examples.en: We might dress up as characters from an old cartoon for the dance.
examples.zh: 舞会上，我们可能会「装扮成」一部老动画里的角色。

collocations: dress up as someone from a film

words.enDefinition: an outfit someone makes for a character or theme

examples.en: The homemade costume looked like a paper lantern from across the room.
examples.zh: 从房间另一头看，那件「自制化装服」像一盏纸灯笼。

examples.en: I wore a homemade costume made from an old pillowcase and ribbon.
examples.zh: 我穿了件用旧枕套和丝带做的「自制化装服」。

words.enDefinition: a costume theme shared by several people dressing up together

examples.en: Our history class planned a group costume based on an old painting.
examples.zh: 我们历史课的同学照着一幅老油画，策划了个「多人配套化装」。

examples.en: The group costume worked because everyone borrowed something in the same colour.
examples.zh: 大家借来的东西都是同一个颜色，所以「多人配套化装」的效果不错。

collocations: take part in a group costume

words.enDefinition: an event where people exchange costumes they no longer use

examples.en: Our hall held a costume swap so students could reuse last year's outfits.
examples.zh: 我们宿舍办了场「化装服交换活动」，让同学能再利用去年的服装。

examples.en: I traded an old hat for a cloak at the costume swap.
examples.zh: 我在「化装服交换活动」上用一顶旧帽子换了件斗篷。

collocations: bring a costume to a costume swap

words.enDefinition: a service that lends costumes for payment for a limited time

examples.en: We looked for costume rental after deciding our matching outfits would cost too much.
examples.zh: 我们觉得买配套服装太贵，就去找「化装服租赁」服务。

examples.en: The drama society offers costume rental from its collection of old stage outfits.
examples.zh: 戏剧社拿珍藏的旧戏服提供「化装服租赁」。

words.enDefinition: small extras used to complete the look of a costume

examples.en: I borrowed costume accessories from the drama society instead of buying a costume.
examples.zh: 我从戏剧社借了「化装服配件」，省得买一套服装。

examples.en: The shop kept its costume accessories in a small box by the register.
examples.zh: 店家把「化装服配件」放在收银台旁边的小盒子里。

words.enDefinition: colouring applied to the skin for decoration or a costume

examples.en: I used blue face paint to match the sleeves of my costume.
examples.zh: 我用了蓝色的「面部彩绘颜料」，和化装服的袖子相配。

examples.en: She borrowed some face paint to draw spots on her own cheeks.
examples.zh: 她借了点「面部彩绘颜料」，在自己脸颊上画斑点。

words.enDefinition: a covering worn over the face as part of an outfit

examples.en: I made a costume mask that looked like a fox for the party.
examples.zh: 我为派对做了一个狐狸样子的「化装面具」。

examples.en: He lifted his costume mask so I could recognise him in the photograph.
examples.zh: 他掀起「化装面具」，好让我能在照片里认出他。

words.enDefinition: a hairpiece worn to look like a character or someone else

examples.en: The red costume wig gave my roommate an entirely different look.
examples.zh: 那顶红色「化装假发」让室友看起来像是完全变了个人。

examples.en: I borrowed a costume wig from the drama department for the student party.
examples.zh: 我从戏剧系借了顶「化装假发」，准备参加学生派对。

words.enDefinition: to cut decoration into a pumpkin, often for Halloween

examples.en: Our host offered to show us how to carve a pumpkin after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后，寄宿家庭主人主动说要给我们示范怎么「雕刻南瓜」。

examples.en: We planned to carve a pumpkin in the shape of a smiling owl.
examples.zh: 我们打算「雕刻南瓜」，把它刻成一只微笑的猫头鹰。

words.enDefinition: a competition for the best designs cut into pumpkins

examples.en: My flatmate entered the pumpkin carving contest with a design of our library.
examples.zh: 室友用我们图书馆的图案参加了「南瓜雕刻比赛」。

examples.en: The pumpkin carving contest winners had their pumpkins displayed in the student centre.
examples.zh: 「南瓜雕刻比赛」获奖者的南瓜摆在学生中心展示。

words.enDefinition: a pumpkin cut into a face or design and lit inside

examples.en: Our jack-o'-lantern had a crooked smile, but everyone liked it.
examples.zh: 我们的「南瓜灯」笑得有点歪，但大家都很喜欢。

examples.en: A glowing jack-o'-lantern stood on the steps outside my friend's apartment.
examples.zh: 朋友公寓门外的台阶上摆着一个发亮的「南瓜灯」。

words.enDefinition: the activity of decorating pumpkins by applying paint to the surface

examples.en: The art club put on a pumpkin painting workshop during lunch.
examples.zh: 美术社在午餐时间办了一场「南瓜彩绘」活动。

examples.en: We tried pumpkin painting because we wanted to cover the pumpkins in dots.
examples.zh: 我们想给南瓜画满圆点，所以尝试了「南瓜彩绘」。

words.enDefinition: a template used to transfer a design onto a surface for carving

examples.en: I used a carving stencil to make a neat owl on mine.
examples.zh: 我用「雕刻描图模板」在自己的南瓜上做了只轮廓整齐的猫头鹰。

examples.en: The club printed a carving stencil with the outline of our campus bell.
examples.zh: 社团印了一张带校园钟轮廓的「雕刻描图模板」。

words.enDefinition: to remove seeds from the inside of something using a scoop

examples.en: My roommate volunteered to scoop out the seeds while I chose a pumpkin design.
examples.zh: 我选南瓜图案时，室友主动帮忙「舀出里面的籽」。

examples.en: We each had a bowl to use when we helped scoop out the seeds.
examples.zh: 我们每人都有一个碗，供帮忙「舀出里面的籽」时用。

collocations: use a spoon to scoop out the seeds

words.enDefinition: a small light made to resemble a candle without a flame

examples.en: I put a flameless candle inside the pumpkin that sat in my window.
examples.zh: 我在窗台上的南瓜里放了一支「无焰蜡烛」。

examples.en: The desk handed out a flameless candle to each student who painted a pumpkin.
examples.zh: 服务台给每位画南瓜的同学都发了一支「无焰蜡烛」。

words.enDefinition: a field where pumpkins grow, often open for visitors to pick

examples.en: We took the bus to a pumpkin patch just outside town.
examples.zh: 我们坐公交去了镇外的一个「南瓜园」。

examples.en: Our campus group visited a pumpkin patch with a farm stand nearby.
examples.zh: 我们学校的小组去了一家「南瓜园」，附近有一个农场小摊。

collocations: take a trip to a pumpkin patch
choose a pumpkin at a pumpkin patch

words.enDefinition: a gourd grown to be displayed for its shape or colour

examples.en: A striped ornamental gourd sat beside the apples at the farm stand.
examples.zh: 农场小摊的苹果旁摆着一个有条纹的「观赏葫芦」。

examples.en: I bought a tiny ornamental gourd to put on my windowsill.
examples.zh: 我买了个小小的「观赏葫芦」，准备放在窗台上。

words.enDefinition: an event celebrating autumn with seasonal activities or local goods

examples.en: The fall festival on our campus had live music and a pumpkin display.
examples.zh: 校园的「秋季庆典」有现场音乐，还展出了南瓜。

examples.en: We bought tickets for the fall festival near my roommate's hometown.
examples.zh: 我们买了室友老家附近「秋季庆典」的门票。

words.enDefinition: an event celebrating the gathering of seasonal crops

examples.en: The harvest festival had a stall where growers talked about their crops.
examples.zh: 「丰收庆典」上有个摊位，种植户在那里介绍自家的作物。

examples.en: Students helped hang banners for the community harvest festival on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六，同学们帮忙为社区的「丰收庆典」挂横幅。

collocations: take part in a harvest festival

words.enDefinition: a short pause in university classes during the autumn term

examples.en: I stayed in town over fall break and explored the nearby trails.
examples.zh: 「秋季假期」我留在镇上，去附近的步道逛了逛。

examples.en: Our fall break was short, so my neighbour took a day trip.
examples.zh: 我们的「秋季假期」很短，所以邻居就出门玩了一天。

collocations: stay on campus over fall break

words.enDefinition: the leaves that change colour and create autumn scenery

examples.en: We took the train north to see the fall foliage along the river.
examples.zh: 我们坐火车往北走，去看河边的「秋叶景色」。

examples.en: The residence newsletter suggested a hike with good views of fall foliage.
examples.zh: 宿舍简报推荐了一条能看到好看「秋叶景色」的徒步路线。

words.enDefinition: the activity of going to see leaves changing colour in autumn

examples.en: A few of us went leaf peeping after the morning club meeting.
examples.zh: 社团上午开完会后，我们几个人出门「观赏秋叶」。

examples.en: I'd never heard of leaf peeping before my roommate invited me along.
examples.zh: 室友叫我一起去之前，我没听说过「观赏秋叶」这项活动。

words.enDefinition: the period when autumn leaves display their most vivid colours

examples.en: We didn't reach the park until a week after peak fall color.
examples.zh: 我们到公园时，已经过了「秋叶色彩最盛期」一周。

examples.en: The student outdoors club planned a weekend hike around peak fall color.
examples.zh: 学生户外社选在「秋叶色彩最盛期」前后安排了周末徒步。

words.enDefinition: indicates that the leaves are less colourful than at their best

examples.en: The website said the leaves were past peak near the lake.
examples.zh: 网站说，湖边的秋叶「已过最佳观赏期」。

examples.en: The valley was past peak by the time our reading week began.
examples.zh: 我们的阅读周开始时，山谷的秋叶「已过最佳观赏期」。

collocations: report that foliage is past peak

words.enDefinition: a prediction of where and when autumn leaves will change colour

examples.en: We checked the foliage forecast before choosing which park to visit.
examples.zh: 选去哪座公园之前，我们看了看「秋叶观赏预报」。

examples.en: The foliage forecast mentioned two nearby trails where leaves were already changing.
examples.zh: 「秋叶观赏预报」提到，附近有两条步道的树叶已经开始变色了。

words.enDefinition: says that leaves are changing colour as autumn arrives

examples.en: Our neighbour said the leaves are turning already along the footpath near her house.
examples.zh: 邻居说，她家附近那条小路旁的「树叶已经开始变色了」。

examples.en: The leaves are turning near the river, so we might take a walk tomorrow.
examples.zh: 河边的「树叶开始变色了」，所以我们明天可能会去散步。

collocations: see that the leaves are turning

words.enDefinition: the first occurrence of frost in autumn in a particular place

examples.en: Our garden group took pictures of the first frost before class.
examples.zh: 上课前，我们园艺小组拍了「初霜」的照片。

examples.en: The first frost arrived while the pumpkins were still on our porch.
examples.zh: 降「初霜」的时候，南瓜还摆在我们的门廊上。

words.enDefinition: fallen leaves collected or gathered together in one place

examples.en: My neighbour's children kept running into the pile of leaves in the yard.
examples.zh: 邻居家的孩子不停地跑进院子里那「一堆落叶」里。

examples.en: A gust blew the pile of leaves back onto the freshly cleared path.
examples.zh: 一阵风把那「一堆落叶」又吹到了刚扫干净的小路上。

collocations: jump into a pile of leaves

words.enDefinition: cool fresh air that is typical of an autumn day

examples.en: We walked back through campus to enjoy the crisp fall air before dark.
examples.zh: 我们穿过校园走回去，趁天黑前享受一下「清爽的秋日空气」。

examples.en: A long walk in the crisp fall air woke me up before class.
examples.zh: 上课前，我在「清爽的秋日空气」里走了很久，人也清醒了。

collocations: walk in the crisp fall air

words.enDefinition: the activity of gathering apples directly from trees at an orchard

examples.en: The students went apple picking together on the first cool Saturday of term.
examples.zh: 学期里第一个凉爽的周六，大家一起去「摘苹果」。

examples.en: I tried apple picking with my roommate's family during a visit home.
examples.zh: 室友回家时我跟着去做客，和他们一家体验了「摘苹果」。

words.enDefinition: an orchard where visitors can pick their own fruit

examples.en: We bought the apples by weight at the U-pick orchard near town.
examples.zh: 我们在镇附近的「自摘果园」按重量买了苹果。

examples.en: The U-pick orchard kept a board showing which varieties were ready.
examples.zh: 「自摘果园」立了块牌子，写着哪些品种已经可以采摘。

words.enDefinition: a place where apples are pressed and made into cider

examples.en: The cider mill let us watch the apples go into the press.
examples.zh: 「苹果汁作坊」让我们观看苹果被送进压榨机的过程。

examples.en: We stopped at a cider mill on our way back to campus.
examples.zh: 我们回学校时，顺路去了家「苹果汁作坊」。

words.enDefinition: a network of paths cut through a field of corn

examples.en: We took the short route through the corn maze before it rained.
examples.zh: 下雨前，我们选了穿过「玉米地迷宫」的短路线。

examples.en: My roommate laughed when we got lost in the corn maze again.
examples.zh: 我们又在「玉米地迷宫」里迷路时，室友笑了起来。

collocations: find your way through a corn maze
get lost in a corn maze

words.enDefinition: a recreational ride in a wagon carrying straw or hay

examples.en: Our hayride ended at a field full of small orange pumpkins.
examples.zh: 我们「乘干草车游览」的终点是一块长满橙色小南瓜的地。

examples.en: We took a hayride with students from the hall next door.
examples.zh: 我们和隔壁宿舍楼的同学一起「乘干草车游览」。

words.enDefinition: a hayride with staged scary scenes along the route

examples.en: I liked the silly costumes on the haunted hayride more than the scares.
examples.zh: 比起「惊吓主题干草车游览」上吓人的环节，我更喜欢那些搞怪的化装服。

examples.en: Our group booked a haunted hayride after hearing about it in class.
examples.zh: 我们组在课堂上听人提起「惊吓主题干草车游览」，随后订了票。

words.enDefinition: dried grass packed tightly into a block or round bundle

examples.en: I sat on a hay bale while my friends picked their pumpkins.
examples.zh: 朋友选南瓜时，我坐在一个「干草捆」上。

examples.en: The volunteers put a hay bale beside the entrance for photographs.
examples.zh: 志愿者在入口旁放了一个「干草捆」，供大家拍照。

words.enDefinition: a human-shaped figure used in fields or as a decoration

examples.en: Our class built a scarecrow for the fall festival at the farm.
examples.zh: 我们班做了个「稻草人」，放在农场的秋季庆典上。

examples.en: The scarecrow near the corn maze wore a faded university sweatshirt.
examples.zh: 玉米地迷宫附近的「稻草人」穿着件褪了色的大学卫衣。

words.zhGloss: 可接触动物的小动物园
words.enDefinition: a place where visitors can touch some of the animals
acceptedZhAnswers: 可接触动物的小动物园

examples.en: The farm festival had a petting zoo near the pumpkin field.
examples.zh: 农场庆典在南瓜地旁设了个「可接触动物的小动物园」。

examples.en: My host family's kids wanted to see goats at the petting zoo.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的孩子想在「可接触动物的小动物园」看山羊。

words.enDefinition: an autumn holiday for giving thanks in North America

examples.en: Some of us spent Thanksgiving on campus and shared a meal.
examples.zh: 我们几个留在学校过「感恩节」，一起吃了顿饭。

examples.en: I called my family on Thanksgiving before joining friends for dinner.
examples.zh: 「感恩节」那天，我先给家人打了电话，再和朋友吃晚饭。

words.enDefinition: the United States holiday on the fourth Thursday in November

examples.en: I first experienced American Thanksgiving with a friend's family in Ohio.
examples.zh: 我第一次过「美国感恩节」是在俄亥俄州，和一个朋友的家人一起过的。

examples.en: My friends in the States were planning their American Thanksgiving trip in November.
examples.zh: 我在美国的朋友正在筹备十一月「美国感恩节」的出行。

words.enDefinition: the Canadian holiday on the second Monday in October

examples.en: Our Toronto neighbours invited us to dinner for Canadian Thanksgiving in October.
examples.zh: 十月，多伦多的邻居邀请我们一同吃「加拿大感恩节」晚餐。

examples.en: I marked Canadian Thanksgiving on my calendar when I moved to Ottawa.
examples.zh: 搬到渥太华时，我在日历上标出了「加拿大感恩节」。

words.enDefinition: a break in classes around the Thanksgiving holiday

examples.en: I took the train home for Thanksgiving break and saw my sister.
examples.zh: 我坐火车回家过「感恩节假期」，见到了妹妹。

examples.en: My advisor asked what I planned to do during Thanksgiving break this November.
examples.zh: 导师问我，十一月的「感恩节假期」打算做什么。

collocations: stay on campus over Thanksgiving break

words.enDefinition: the weekend around the date of Thanksgiving

examples.en: We spent Thanksgiving weekend with a classmate's family just outside Montreal.
examples.zh: 我们在蒙特利尔城外和同学的家人一起过了「感恩节周末」。

examples.en: The club plans to go hiking over Thanksgiving weekend if it stays dry.
examples.zh: 如果不下雨，社团打算在「感恩节周末」去徒步。

words.enDefinition: a special meal shared with others to celebrate Thanksgiving

examples.en: We joined my roommate's family for Thanksgiving dinner at their apartment.
examples.zh: 我们去了室友家的公寓，和他们一家一起吃「感恩节晚餐」。

examples.en: The students took a group picture before Thanksgiving dinner in the lounge.
examples.zh: 同学们在休息室吃「感恩节晚餐」前拍了张合影。

words.enDefinition: a Thanksgiving-style meal or celebration shared among friends

examples.en: We held Friendsgiving because several roommates were staying in town.
examples.zh: 因为好几个室友留在镇上，我们办了场「朋友感恩节聚餐」。

examples.en: The international student club invited everyone to Friendsgiving in the lounge.
examples.zh: 国际学生社团邀请大家到休息室参加「朋友感恩节聚餐」。

words.enDefinition: to contribute some food that others at the meal can try

examples.en: Guests at Friendsgiving could bring a dish to share if they wanted to contribute.
examples.zh: 参加朋友感恩节聚餐的人想出份力，可以「带道菜和大家分享」。

examples.en: My roommate offered to bring a dish to share instead of bringing another bottle of juice.
examples.zh: 室友主动提出「带道菜和大家分享」，省得再带一瓶果汁。

collocations: ask everyone to bring a dish to share
offer to bring a dish to share
choose to bring a dish to share

words.enDefinition: a list for recording what guests will bring to a shared meal

examples.en: The club posted a potluck sign-up sheet for anyone bringing food to dinner.
examples.zh: 社团公布了「自带菜报名表」，供准备带食物来吃晚饭的人填写。

examples.en: I checked the potluck sign-up sheet before deciding whether to bring dessert.
examples.zh: 决定要不要带甜点前，我看了看「自带菜报名表」。

collocations: fill in the potluck sign-up sheet
add your dish to the potluck sign-up sheet

words.enDefinition: room at a meal for one person beyond the expected group

examples.en: My tutor said there was an extra seat at the table if I was staying in town.
examples.zh: 老师说，如果我留在镇上，「餐桌上还有个额外座位」可以给我。

examples.en: Our host arranged an extra seat at the table when my roommate asked to come too.
examples.zh: 室友问能不能也来时，做东的人在「餐桌上加了一个座位」。

collocations: offer an extra seat at the table
find an extra seat at the table
arrange an extra seat at the table

words.enDefinition: the dishes and utensils laid out for one person

examples.en: I laid out one more place setting when a neighbour dropped by.
examples.zh: 有个邻居过来时，我又摆了一套「一人份的餐具」。

examples.en: Each place setting had a handwritten card with the guest's name.
examples.zh: 每套「一人份的摆台餐具」旁都有一张写着客人姓名的手写卡片。

words.enDefinition: a card marking where a particular guest should sit

examples.en: I found my place card next to a little paper pumpkin.
examples.zh: 我在一个小纸南瓜旁找到了自己的「座位名卡」。

examples.en: One student drew a tiny leaf on every place card before dinner.
examples.zh: 饭前，有个同学在每张「座位名卡」上都画了一片小叶子。

words.enDefinition: the planned positions of where different people will sit

examples.en: We changed the seating arrangement so everyone could reach the long table.
examples.zh: 我们改了「座位安排」，这样大家都能坐到长桌旁。

examples.en: Our host kept the seating arrangement informal so guests could move around.
examples.zh: 做东的人把「座位安排」得比较随意，方便客人走动。

words.enDefinition: to prepare an additional seat with dishes and utensils for a meal

examples.en: Could you set another place for my roommate before we start dinner tonight?
examples.zh: 今晚开饭前，你能给我室友「再摆一套餐具」吗？

examples.en: We had to set another place when a friend stopped by unexpectedly.
examples.zh: 有位朋友没提前打招呼就来了，我们得「再摆一套餐具」。

collocations: ask someone to set another place
set another place for a guest

words.enDefinition: tells guests that their meal is ready to eat

examples.en: Our host called "Dinner is served!" as we finished taking the group photo.
examples.zh: 我们拍完合影时，做东的人喊了声「开饭了」！

examples.en: We heard "Dinner is served!" and put our cards away before heading inside.
examples.zh: 我们听见有人说「开饭了」，就把牌收起来，进了屋。

words.enDefinition: to offer shared dishes from which diners serve themselves

examples.en: We chose to serve family-style so people could try what others had brought.
examples.zh: 我们决定「把菜放中间一起夹」，这样大家都能尝尝别人带来的菜。

examples.en: The hosts decided to serve family-style instead of filling plates in the kitchen.
examples.zh: 主人决定「把菜放中间一起夹」，省得在厨房里逐盘给大家盛好。

words.enDefinition: invites someone to take another serving when they want one

examples.en: You can help yourself to seconds once everyone has had their first serving.
examples.zh: 等大家都盛过第一份，「想再吃可以自己添」。

examples.en: My host said, "Help yourself to seconds," when she saw me looking at the potatoes.
examples.zh: 主人看我望着土豆，说：「想再吃可以自己添」。

collocations: feel free to help yourself to seconds
tell guests to help themselves to seconds
you can help yourself to seconds

words.enDefinition: asks other people to begin eating before your group arrives

examples.en: I texted "Start without us," because our bus was running nearly half an hour late.
examples.zh: 公交要晚到将近半小时，我就发消息说「不用等我们，先开饭」。

examples.en: Please start without us if the rest of the class is ready to eat.
examples.zh: 如果班里其他人都准备好了，「不用等我们，先开饭」吧。

collocations: tell them to start without us
go ahead and start without us

words.enDefinition: to eat less at first so you can have dessert later

examples.en: We tried to save room for dessert because three people had brought something sweet.
examples.zh: 三个人都带了甜食，所以我们尽量「留点肚子吃甜点」。

examples.en: My roommate reminded everyone to save room for dessert before passing around the rolls.
examples.zh: 室友把面包卷传给大家之前，提醒大家「留点肚子吃甜点」。

collocations: try to save room for dessert
remember to save room for dessert
tell guests to save room for dessert

words.enDefinition: to hand a large serving plate to someone nearby

examples.en: Could you pass the platter down this way so Maya can try some?
examples.zh: 能不能「把大餐盘递过来」，让玛雅也尝一点？

examples.en: We had to pass the platter carefully because the table was so crowded.
examples.zh: 餐桌上摆得满满当当，我们得小心「把大餐盘递过去」。

collocations: ask someone to pass the platter

words.enDefinition: a large spoon for putting food onto someone else's plate

examples.en: I put a serving spoon beside the dish my roommate had brought.
examples.zh: 我在室友带来的那盘菜旁放了一把「公用盛菜勺」。

examples.en: Someone fetched another serving spoon when the guests opened the second dish.
examples.zh: 客人打开第二盘菜时，有人又拿来一把「公用盛菜勺」。

words.enDefinition: a small pouring container used to serve gravy at meals

examples.en: I passed the gravy boat to the student sitting next to me.
examples.zh: 我把「船形肉汁壶」递给了坐在旁边的同学。

examples.en: A little gravy boat sat between the bread basket and the flowers.
examples.zh: 面包篮和鲜花中间放着一个小小的「船形肉汁壶」。

words.enDefinition: to cut a cooked whole turkey into portions for serving

examples.en: Our host asked her brother to carve the turkey once everyone sat down.
examples.zh: 大家坐好后，主人请自己的兄弟「把火鸡切片分给大家」。

examples.en: My classmate offered to carve the turkey while the rest of us brought plates.
examples.zh: 我们其他人拿餐盘时，同学主动提出「把火鸡切片分给大家」。

collocations: learn how to carve the turkey
ask someone to carve the turkey

words.enDefinition: a bird's forked bone pulled apart in a wishing tradition

examples.en: My host's two children asked if they could pull the wishbone apart after dinner.
examples.zh: 主人家的两个孩子问，能不能吃完饭后拉断「许愿骨」。

examples.en: I had never heard of the wishbone until the students discussed holiday traditions.
examples.zh: 我从没听说过「许愿骨」，直到同学们聊起节日习俗。

words.enDefinition: to express appreciation for good things or other people

examples.en: Our group took a moment to give thanks before we started eating.
examples.zh: 开饭前，我们这组人花了一点时间「表达感恩」。

examples.en: We decided to give thanks for the help we'd received that year.
examples.zh: 我们决定为这一年受到的帮助「表达感恩」。

collocations: take a moment to give thanks

words.enDefinition: to tell others what good things you appreciate

examples.en: The card said, "Say what you're thankful for if you'd like to share something."
examples.zh: 卡片上写着，如果愿意分享，可以「说说你感激什么」。

examples.en: Before dinner our host said, "Say what you're thankful for in one short sentence."
examples.zh: 晚饭前，主人说：「说说你感激什么」，简短一句话就好。

collocations: take a moment to say what you're thankful for
if you'd like to say what you're thankful for
go around the table and say what you're thankful for

words.enDefinition: to say a short prayer before starting a meal

examples.en: My host asked if we could wait while they say grace.
examples.zh: 主人问，我们能否等一下，让他们「作饭前祷告」。

examples.en: The family chose to say grace quietly before bringing the dishes around.
examples.zh: 这家人先安静地「作饭前祷告」，再把菜传给大家。

words.enDefinition: to remember and appreciate the good things in your life

examples.en: My grandmother says it's good to count your blessings once in a while.
examples.zh: 奶奶说，时不时「想想值得感恩的事」挺好的。

examples.en: The prompt said "Count your blessings," so I wrote about my friends here.
examples.zh: 提示写着「想想值得感恩的事」，所以我写了在这儿交的朋友。

collocations: take time to count your blessings

words.enDefinition: a chain of paper strips containing notes of appreciation

examples.en: We added a link to the gratitude chain after our Friendsgiving meal.
examples.zh: 朋友感恩节聚餐后，我们给「感恩纸链」又接了一环。

examples.en: The gratitude chain included messages about friendship, family, and finding a home.
examples.zh: 「感恩纸链」上写着有关友情、家人和找到归属感的话。

collocations: add a link to a gratitude chain

words.enDefinition: to let each person seated at a table speak in turn

examples.en: We decided to go around the table and share one thing we appreciated.
examples.zh: 我们决定「按座位轮流说」，每人分享一件感激的事。

examples.en: Our host asked if we could go around the table to introduce ourselves.
examples.zh: 主人问，我们能不能「按座位轮流说」，做一下自我介绍。

collocations: go around the table before dinner
take a moment to go around the table
ask if we can go around the table

words.enDefinition: to come together beside a table, usually to share a meal

examples.en: We usually gather around the table only after everyone has arrived for the holiday.
examples.zh: 我们一般等过节的人到齐了，才「围坐到餐桌旁」。

examples.en: Our hosts asked us to gather around the table before they brought out dessert.
examples.zh: 主人请我们先「围坐到餐桌旁」，他们再端出甜点。

collocations: ask everyone to gather around the table
gather around the table for dinner
wait for friends to gather around the table

words.enDefinition: to bring home food that remains after a shared meal

examples.en: We asked who wanted to take leftovers home before clearing the table.
examples.zh: 收拾餐桌前，我们先问了谁想「把剩菜带回家」。

examples.en: I didn't plan to take leftovers home, but my neighbour insisted I take some.
examples.zh: 我原本没打算「把剩菜带回家」，但邻居执意让我带一些。

collocations: offer to let guests take leftovers home
ask if you can take leftovers home

words.enDefinition: to divide off a single portion of a pie for serving

examples.en: I offered to cut a slice of pie for my neighbour while she poured the tea.
examples.zh: 邻居倒茶时，我主动帮她「切一块派」。

examples.en: Could you cut a slice of pie for me while you have the plate nearby?
examples.zh: 盘子就在你手边，能帮我「切一块派」吗？

collocations: offer to cut a slice of pie
cut a slice of pie for a guest
ask someone to cut a slice of pie

words.enDefinition: a sweet baked pie filled with a spiced pumpkin mixture

examples.en: Our host served pumpkin pie after everyone finished sharing their holiday stories.
examples.zh: 大家讲完各自的节日故事后，主人端上了「南瓜派」。

examples.en: I had a slice of pumpkin pie at my first Friendsgiving dinner.
examples.zh: 我第一次参加朋友感恩节聚餐时，吃了一块「南瓜派」。

words.enDefinition: a sweet shaped like a corn kernel, associated with Halloween

examples.en: My roommate put a bowl of candy corn beside the welcome sign.
examples.zh: 室友在欢迎牌旁边摆了一碗「玉米粒形糖果」。

examples.en: I'd never seen candy corn until our floor held its costume party.
examples.zh: 我们这层楼办化装派对的时候，我才第一次见到「玉米粒形糖果」。

words.enDefinition: a whole apple covered in caramel, often served on a stick

examples.en: I bought a caramel apple from a stall at the harvest festival.
examples.zh: 我在丰收庆典的一个摊位买了个「裹焦糖的苹果」。

examples.en: My host family's children shared a caramel apple after leaving the corn maze.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭的孩子们走出玉米地迷宫后，分吃了一个「裹焦糖的苹果」。

words.enDefinition: warm apple juice, often spiced, served as a seasonal drink

examples.en: The farm shop served hot apple cider next to the entrance to the maze.
examples.zh: 那家农场店在迷宫入口旁供应「热苹果汁」。

examples.en: We drank hot apple cider outside while our friends picked out a pumpkin.
examples.zh: 朋友选南瓜时，我们在外面喝着「热苹果汁」。

words.enDefinition: a blend of spices traditionally used to flavour pumpkin pie

examples.en: The café had a sign for drinks flavoured with pumpkin spice this week.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆的牌子上写着，本周有用「南瓜派香料混合物」调味的饮品。

examples.en: One of my classmates brought cookies that smelled like pumpkin spice.
examples.zh: 一位同学带来了饼干，闻起来有「南瓜派香料混合物」的味道。

words.enDefinition: a procession held on the day of Thanksgiving

examples.en: A few of us watched the Thanksgiving Day parade while everyone prepared dinner.
examples.zh: 大家忙着准备晚饭时，我们几个人看了「感恩节游行」。

examples.en: We heard drums from the Thanksgiving Day parade before we reached the main street.
examples.zh: 还没走到大街，我们就听到了「感恩节游行」的鼓声。

words.enDefinition: a decorated vehicle that carries people or displays in a procession

examples.en: The art students built a parade float with enormous painted maple leaves.
examples.zh: 美术生做了一辆「游行花车」，上面有巨大的彩绘枫叶。

examples.en: My neighbour waved from a parade float during the Thanksgiving celebration.
examples.zh: 感恩节庆典上，邻居在一辆「游行花车」上向我挥手。

words.enDefinition: a large inflatable figure in the shape of a recognisable character

examples.en: The first character balloon I saw in the parade looked like a duck.
examples.zh: 我在游行上看到的第一个「卡通角色形气球」长得像只鸭子。

examples.en: My little cousin pointed to a character balloon above the marching band.
examples.zh: 我的小表亲指着行进乐队上方的一个「卡通角色形气球」。

words.enDefinition: a community running or walking event around Thanksgiving, especially in America

examples.en: My friend signed up for a Turkey Trot near her campus in Illinois.
examples.zh: 朋友报名参加了伊利诺伊州校园附近的「感恩节趣味跑」。

examples.en: We walked most of the Turkey Trot and met other students there.
examples.zh: 「感恩节趣味跑」的大部分路程我们都是走的，还在那里认识了别的同学。

collocations: sign up for a Turkey Trot

words.enDefinition: an American football game played around the holiday of Thanksgiving

examples.en: My roommate's family watched a Thanksgiving football game after they finished lunch.
examples.zh: 室友一家吃完午饭后，看了一场「感恩节美式橄榄球赛」。

examples.en: Some students came early to watch the Thanksgiving football game in the lounge.
examples.zh: 一些同学早点来了，在休息室看「感恩节美式橄榄球赛」。

words.enDefinition: a holiday meal organised for people in a local community

examples.en: I helped set tables for the community Thanksgiving meal at our local centre.
examples.zh: 我在社区中心帮忙为「社区感恩节聚餐」摆桌。

examples.en: Our class was invited to the community Thanksgiving meal near the new library.
examples.zh: 我们班受邀参加新图书馆附近的「社区感恩节聚餐」。

collocations: serve at a community Thanksgiving meal

words.enDefinition: a package of ingredients or food for preparing a holiday meal

examples.en: A few students helped pack a holiday meal kit for each registered household.
examples.zh: 几位同学帮忙给每户报名的家庭打包一份「节日餐食包」。

examples.en: I picked up a holiday meal kit from the organisation hosting the dinner.
examples.zh: 我从负责晚餐的机构那里领了一份「节日餐食包」。

collocations: hand out a holiday meal kit

words.enDefinition: an event where people can get a turkey without paying

examples.en: The student volunteers helped families check in for the turkey giveaway.
examples.zh: 学生志愿者协助各家到「免费发放火鸡活动」签到。

examples.en: Our neighbour told us about a turkey giveaway at the community centre.
examples.zh: 邻居告诉我们，社区中心有一场「免费发放火鸡活动」。

words.enDefinition: a period when many people travel around the Thanksgiving holiday

examples.en: I left a little early to avoid the Thanksgiving travel rush that week.
examples.zh: 那周我稍微早一点出发，避开「感恩节出行高峰」。

examples.en: The station felt busier than usual during the Thanksgiving travel rush last November.
examples.zh: 去年十一月的「感恩节出行高峰」期间，车站感觉比平时更忙。

collocations: ahead of the Thanksgiving travel rush

words.enDefinition: the opening hours that a business uses during a holiday

examples.en: The campus shop posted its holiday hours on the door before Thanksgiving.
examples.zh: 感恩节前，校园商店把「节日营业时间」贴在了门上。

examples.en: I checked the holiday hours because I needed to buy groceries before dinner.
examples.zh: 我晚饭前得买些食品杂货，所以查了一下「节日营业时间」。

words.enDefinition: a contest that compares pumpkins to see which is heaviest

examples.en: People crowded around the scale to watch the pumpkin weigh-off on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六，人们围着秤看「南瓜重量比赛」。

examples.en: My classmate brought his biggest pumpkin to the county fair's pumpkin weigh-off.
examples.zh: 同学把自己最大的南瓜带去参加县集市的「南瓜重量比赛」。

words.enDefinition: the time of year when crops are gathered from fields

examples.en: The campus garden held a picnic near the end of harvest season.
examples.zh: 「收获季」快结束时，校园菜园办了一场野餐。

examples.en: Our campus farm ran extra walking tours during harvest season that year.
examples.zh: 那年「收获季」，校园农场加开了几次步行参观。

words.enDefinition: a shared evening meal celebrating the end of a harvest

examples.en: The community garden hosted a harvest supper using vegetables from its plots.
examples.zh: 社区菜园用自家地块种的菜办了一场「丰收聚餐」。

examples.en: I helped put chairs out for the harvest supper in the hall.
examples.zh: 我帮忙给礼堂里举行的「丰收聚餐」摆椅子。

words.enDefinition: a ring of seasonal materials used as an autumn decoration

examples.en: Our hall made a fall wreath out of dried leaves and ribbon.
examples.zh: 我们宿舍楼用干叶子和丝带做了一个「秋季装饰花环」。

examples.en: I saw an orange fall wreath on the door of my friend's house.
examples.zh: 我在朋友家门上看见一个橙色的「秋季装饰花环」。

words.enDefinition: a decoration placed prominently in the middle of a table

examples.en: We used painted gourds and a small vase as our table centerpiece.
examples.zh: 我们用彩绘葫芦和一个小花瓶做「餐桌中央的装饰」。

examples.en: The table centerpiece was so tall that I couldn't see across the table.
examples.zh: 「餐桌中央的装饰」太高了，我都看不见桌对面。

words.enDefinition: a game of catching floating apples with your mouth

examples.en: Our hall played a game of bobbing for apples at its autumn party.
examples.zh: 我们宿舍楼的秋季派对玩了「用嘴捞苹果游戏」。

examples.en: I had never seen bobbing for apples before the fall festival on campus.
examples.zh: 在学校办秋季庆典前，我没见过「用嘴捞苹果游戏」。

collocations: play a game of bobbing for apples

words.enDefinition: an organised walk in which participants show what they are wearing

examples.en: The evening began with a costume parade through the main residence hall.
examples.zh: 晚上的活动从穿过主宿舍楼的「化装游行」开始。

examples.en: I watched the costume parade from the steps with two other students.
examples.zh: 我和另外两个同学在台阶上看了「化装游行」。

words.enDefinition: a small bag used to hold candy or other treats

examples.en: One of the children dropped a treat bag beside the mailbox.
examples.zh: 一个小孩把「装节日糖果的袋子」掉在了信箱旁边。

examples.en: The student café put one cookie in each treat bag before closing.
examples.zh: 学生咖啡馆关门前，往每个「装节日糖果的袋子」里放了一块曲奇。

words.enDefinition: a narrow tube that gives off light when activated

examples.en: The volunteers gave each child a glow stick at the Halloween event.
examples.zh: 万圣节活动上，志愿者给每个小孩发了一根「荧光棒」。

examples.en: She held a green glow stick so we could find her easily.
examples.zh: 她拿着一根绿色的「荧光棒」，这样我们就容易找到她。

words.enDefinition: a tall pointed hat associated with costumes of fictional witches

examples.en: I wore a witch's hat to the evening film at our residence.
examples.zh: 晚上宿舍放映电影时，我戴了顶「女巫帽」。

examples.en: My roommate's witch's hat was too tall for the group picture.
examples.zh: 室友的「女巫帽」太高，合影都不好拍。

words.enDefinition: pointed false teeth worn as part of a vampire costume

examples.en: I took out my vampire fangs before trying to eat the cookies.
examples.zh: 我先摘下「吸血鬼假尖牙」，再试着吃曲奇。

examples.en: Her vampire fangs made it hard to smile in the group photo.
examples.zh: 她戴着「吸血鬼假尖牙」，拍合影时很难露出笑容。
